risks: InkPuppet.place() rewrites outer's transform on every frame, so horizontal travel must never be animated on outer. Travel is expressed by sliding the world group past a fixed figure; facing is expressed by scaleX on the actor group, which place() does not touch.

The catalog has no 'stands still, confused' clip, which is the emotional centre of the piece. Mitigation: shuffle reads as aimless searching, and the confusion is carried by the empty hand, the stillness and the one speech balloon. If the contact sheet disagrees, extend with ink-theater/mocap/add-motion.mjs — GitHub is reachable from here.

A mocap clip loops to fill its segment duration, so a segment much longer than the clip visibly repeats. Keep walk segments near a multiple of the clip length and break long travel with a different clip.
The figure has no face, so no emotion can be played on it. Every emotional beat has to be staged instead.

metadata.source: svg_rig_builder produced the first draft. It was replaced here because the tool's default scaffold assumes a cartoon rig with a mouth and pupils, and the rig that actually renders is ink-theater/ink-puppet.js — six hand-drawn paths posed from motion capture. Recording the generic scaffold as the plan would have made the artifact a fiction. character-animation is marked beta and this is the kind of rough edge that comes with that.
metadata.joints_note: The pivots above are the neutral STAND pose from ink-puppet.js, in figure-local units with hips at the origin. They are the pose the draw-in reveals and the pose every clip departs from; they are not keyframes. During a clip, all sixteen joints are supplied per frame by the baked motion capture and written straight onto the six paths — no IK solve, no interpolation, nothing to tune.

sit.description: sits down defeated, and stands back up on its own before the last beat

metadata.source: pose_library_builder produced the first draft. It was replaced because its default poses (blink, look_left, surprised) describe a face this character does not have. A mocap-driven figure has no pose library in the usual sense — it has one neutral pose and a list of clips.
metadata.clip_repeat_check: walk is used twice and never back to back; shuffle separates them and the second is mirrored.

findings.note: svg_rig_builder and pose_library_builder both emitted their generic cartoon scaffold — a rig with a mouth and pupils, and poses like blink and look_left. This character has no face. Both artifacts were rewritten to describe ink-puppet.js's six paths and the mocap clip list; keeping the scaffold would have made the artifacts fiction.
Four risks surfaced before asset work, including the one that actually shaped the composition: place() rewrites the transform every frame, so travel has to move the world instead of the figure.
